text: The runtime engine executes task plans in dependency order, records events for every task and saves a checkpoint when a task fails.
The planner produces a task plan and validates duplicate ids, unknown dependencies, cycles and depth limits before execution.
The MCP server exposes tools over JSON-RPC with bearer token authentication, schema validation and SSRF protection.
Dangerous tools require human approval stored in the event log with a time-to-live and explicit reject support.
The event store persists sessions, runs, tasks, events and checkpoints in memory or inside SQLite.
Observability derives a span tree, run summary, JSONL export and Prometheus metrics from the event log.
RAG chunks documents, embeds them with a hashing embedder and reports recall at k, MRR and nDCG for evaluation.
The multimodal app manages dataset versions, train validation splits and LoRA experiment records.
Security policies block private addresses, block metadata hosts and require HTTPS for remote endpoints.
A checkpoint records completed task ids, outputs, attempts, planner version and model version for recovery.
Deployment reads events and metrics from the runtime, exports logs and reports run summaries to dashboards.
Testing covers failure handling, resume after a failed checkpoint and dependency order in the runtime engine.
The HTTP API uses bearer token authentication and schema validation for every request body.
Data preparation manages dataset versions, validation splits and experiment records for training.
The benchmark measures recall and MRR of the retrieval pipeline against a small golden set.
